correctness.rationale: All length<=3 patterns and 4-patterns of types (4,0),(3,1) are determined by capped Parikh counts. Balanced 4-pattern membership is equivalent to sharing a 3-subsequence with an ordinary balanced 4-subsequence, because a deficient letter can always be inserted when both counts are at least 2. The six-by-six table yields precisely seven formal missing sets; an extra zero/one obstructs two singleton types; explicit witnesses attain all others. The 25 capped-count cells contribute 16+6+24+20=66. Exact fixed-length cap-cell enumeration gives 1,2,3,4,10,16,21,26,31 then 31 forever. Checker enumerated all 8191 binary words through length 12 and validated all 66 witnesses by a direct per-pattern definition. Infinite assertions depend on the proof rather than finite experiments.

The result computes the complete exact index, a canonical finite classification, every fixed-length class count and its first permanent saturation, not merely a restatement of finite index or a computational curiosity. These invariants directly characterize discriminatory power of bounded jumbled-subsequence signatures. Results are modest in parameter scope and do not claim a general theory.
